Check that a fitted network solves its estimator

Source: R/certificate.R
certificate.Rd

certificate() measures how far a fitted network is from the solution of its estimator. For a regularized or constrained estimator such as the graphical lasso, this is the largest violation of the optimality (Karush–Kuhn–Tucker) conditions; a value near zero means the network is the optimum, up to numerical precision.

Such an estimator defines the network as the solution of an optimization problem; the graphical lasso, for example, maximizes a penalized likelihood. Any solution must satisfy the problem's optimality conditions, so whether a returned network is that solution can be checked without a second solver; the amount by which the network violates the conditions is its certificate. The information-filtering (TMFG) and relative-importance networks are not optima of an objective; for them the certificate checks the identity that defines the graph. A network changed after fitting, by a threshold or by pruning, is no longer the solution that was checked, and its certificate is reported as missing.

certificate() returns the value together with the kind of certificate and whether it falls below a tolerance.

Correlation and partial-correlation networks involve no optimization and have no certificate. To check a precision matrix or regression coefficients that are not stored in a fitted network, call glasso_kkt(), ggm_support_kkt() or glm_lasso_kkt() directly.

Usage

certificate(x, tol = 1e-06)

Arguments

x

A fitted network, an object of class psychnet (psychnet).

tol

Tolerance at or below which the network is reported as certified: a single finite number >= 0. Default 1e-6.

Value

A data frame with one row and columns method (the estimator), certificate (the violation; smaller is better), kind ("kkt" for an optimality certificate, "structural" for TMFG and relative importance, "none" for correlation and partial-correlation networks) and certified (TRUE when certificate is at or below tol). For a network changed after fitting, or a fit that did not converge, certificate and certified are NA. For correlation and partial-correlation networks certificate is NA and certified is TRUE, because no optimization claim is made.

Details

The optimality certificates are computed by glasso_kkt() (graphical lasso networks), ggm_support_kkt() (unregularized networks restricted to a graph) and glm_lasso_kkt() (nodewise Ising and mixed graphical models). The structural certificates are tmfg_certificate(), the number of violated TMFG properties (0 to 4), and lmg_certificate(), the largest difference between the summed importance shares of a node's predictors and that node's explained variance.

Conditions

psychnet_bad_input when x is not a psychnet network or tol is not a single finite number >= 0.

See also

glasso_kkt(), ggm_support_kkt(), glm_lasso_kkt(), tmfg_certificate() and lmg_certificate() for the individual checks; psychnet() for the estimators.

Examples

S <- 0.4^abs(outer(1:6, 1:6, "-"))
certificate(ebic_glasso(cor_matrix = S, n = 250))
#>   method certificate kind certified
#> 1 glasso 1.10463e-10  kkt      TRUE
certificate(tmfg_network(cor_matrix = S))
#>   method certificate       kind certified
#> 1   tmfg           0 structural      TRUE
